Steps: 1) Fetch full ticket details for T-1070 with get_ticket to confirm the service (payroll) and impact scope. 2) Call get_escalation_matrix for the payroll service to find the correct severity for a company-wide/all-users impact, and set that severity on the ticket with set_severity (do not guess). 3) If the ticket has no SLA deadline yet, set one using extend_sla to current time (fetched via get_current_time) plus the response target for that severity from the matrix; if it already has a committed deadline, do not move it earlier. 4) Determine which rotation owns payroll per the matrix, and which rotation the matrix names for escalation at this severity. 5) Resolve who is on call for that escalation rotation at the ticket's SLA deadline instant (use get_oncall with an explicit `at` equal to the deadline, not the current time) and escalate the ticket to that engineer via escalate_ticket with a one-sentence reason citing the payroll outage and its severity. 6) Before considering closure, check the ticket's linked tickets (from get_ticket) - if any linked ticket is still open (not closed/merged), do NOT close T-1070; instead post a comment on T-1070 explicitly naming the blocking linked ticket and stating the ticket cannot be closed today until that one resolves, leaving it in escalated status for the next shift. 7) If there are no open linked tickets blocking it, still do not close it unilaterally without evidence the payroll run was actually fixed - since this is a live phone report with no confirmed fix, post a comment summarizing the severity grading, SLA deadline, and escalation target/engineer, explicitly noting the ticket is being left open/escalated (not closed) for the next shift to pick up with the on-call escalation engineer as current owner. Throughout, strictly follow policy: never guess severity, never assign outside the owning rotation, never move a committed SLA earlier, and never close over an open linked ticket.
